path.description: Database file; relative paths resolve against the application directory

WaitDelayerDefinition.description: Configuration object for selecting and parameterizing a `WaitDelayer` from the registry.

interval.description: Base interval in milliseconds passed to the delayer factory.

autoCreateTable.description: Create the queue table on init

database.description: Services giving the same database name share one handle

idleDelayer.description:
Delayer between two receives of the main consumer while the queue returns no message

Queues answering immediately when empty (PostgresQueue, AMQPQueue...) would otherwise be polled in a tight
loop. The delay grows with the consecutive empty receives, up to `maxIdleDelay`; the time spent in the receive
is deducted, so long-polling queues (SQSQueue, FileQueue, MemoryQueue with a timeout) are not slowed down.

maxConsumers.description:
Max number of queue consumers
Queue will auto increase to this max number if queue is loaded
and it will decrease to just one consumer if no messages are available

maxIdleDelay.description:
Maximum delay between two receives while the queue stays empty, in milliseconds

It bounds the extra latency of the first message after an idle period, and the polling rate of an idle
consumer (4 receives per second at 250ms).

persistence.description: Omitted: in-memory queue, lost on stop(); set: file database, messages survive restarts

table.description: Table backing the queue, created on init

visibilityTimeout.description: Seconds a received but not deleted message stays invisible before being delivered again

waitTime.description:
Seconds an empty receiveMessage waits for a message before returning (long polling): a message sent by this
process ends the wait at once, one written by another process is seen at the end of it

workerDelayer.description: Delayer between two failed attempts to process messages

workerParallelism.description: Define if worker should process multi message received in //

path.description: Database file; relative paths resolve against the application directory

readOnly.description: Open the file read-only: writes are rejected with a WebdaError

tables#2.description:
Per-model table name overrides.
Maps a model identifier (e.g. "Webda/User") to a custom table name.

typeCheck#2.description: Startup check of the stored types: one WARN listing the legacy, untyped and unknown types found

maxRows.description: Rows scanned at most by stores without a native count; beyond, the counts are "at least"

Schema.description: Parameters of the relational store: those of {@link SQLiteStore} plus the schema layout and lifecycle

aggregationFallback.description:
What to do when an aggregation on this store cannot run natively and must
stream every matching object through memory

autoCreateTable.description: Auto create tables if they do not exist

columnNaming.description: `preserve` keeps the field names as column names (quoted camelCase), `snake_case` converts them

extraColumn.description: JSON column keeping the properties the model schema does not declare, `false` to refuse them

foreignKeys.description: Declare the foreign key constraints between the tables of the store

maxGroups.description: Maximum number of groups an aggregation may produce without LIMIT (or in memory)

numericAsDecimal.description: Declare JSON `number` fields as `DECIMAL` instead of `REAL`

persistence.description:
Omitted: in-memory database, lost on stop() (like MemoryStore without persistence)
Set: file database, every committed write is durable

pragmas.description: Extra PRAGMAs run on open, e.g. { cache_size: -64000 }

schemaSync.description:
What `init()` does with the database schema

- `none`: nothing
- `create`: create the missing tables, with their indexes and inline foreign keys
- `alter`: `create`, plus add the missing columns and indexes of the existing tables (SQLite cannot add a
  foreign key to an existing table: it is reported)
- `validate`: write nothing, fail when anything is missing or differs

slowQueryLogLevel.description: Log level used for slow queries

slowQueryMaxLength.description: Maximum length of the query string written to logs / events (longer queries are truncated)

slowQueryThreshold.description:
Duration in ms above which a query is considered slow.
Set to 0 to disable slow query detection.

strict.description:
Allow to load object that does not have the type data

If set to true, then the Store will only managed the defined _model and no
model extending this one

table.description:
The table of every model of the store, subclasses and models routed to this store as fallback included (the
Webda 3 layout). Without it each model gets its own table (its identifier lowercased with "/" → "_").

tables.description:
Per-model table name overrides.
Maps a model identifier (e.g. "Webda/User") to a custom table name.

transaction.description:
Wrap all statements of an operation in a single transaction

- "none": autocommit per statement
- "operation": BEGIN on the first statement of an operation, COMMIT when the operation succeeds, ROLLBACK when
  it fails. Nested operations join the outermost one; `transaction: false` on an operation opts it out.

typeCheck.description: Startup check of the stored types: one WARN listing the legacy, untyped and unknown types found

Schema.title: SQLiteRelationalStore

sqlite schema.description: Print the relational schema plan, its DDL or the diff with the database

sql.description: Print the CREATE statements of the plan

diff.description: Open the database and print what schemaSync alter would run, and the drift it never resolves
